Planned small at low effort. Diagnosing a flake-gate failure took an Opus-level investigation, and a slow background Fireguard run stalled the low-effort worker twice. Fireguard tickets need either more effort or explicit detached-run instructions.
Sonnet 5.5 medium handled the end-to-end round and the integration fixes, across one restart.

wentPoorly: At least five orchestrator session restarts stopped running workers. They cost DM-135, DM-137, DM-138 and DM-139 one or two attempts each, and made DM-135's test-first order unprovable.

The host catalog was registered with tool names that don't match the plan's (repo_read, repo_write, test_execution), so every claim is recorded as 'Orchestrator (fallback)' with no model. The run's catalog is fixed at start.
A heartbeat without leaseSeconds silently cut a 1 h lease back to the 900 s default, and DM-139 lost an attempt to it.
Workers waiting on long background commands (Fireguard) stalled and let leases lapse twice.
DM-139 used all three attempts. The person asked the orchestrator to do the last one itself, so it had no independent worker review.
Parallel tickets editing the same files (RepositoryView.tsx, source.css, FakeGit) produced merge conflicts, and one bad resolution truncated source.css.
wentWell: Every work ticket landed on the planned model and effort (Sonnet 5.5, medium). None was rejected for quality.
Row checks after each merge kept the combined branch green: typecheck plus up to 3,022 targeted tests at every row.
The acceptance round caught two integration defects that no unit test sees: CSS truncated by a merge, which left the built app unstyled, and 21 dead exports.
Long leases, resuming the same worker after a restart, and running Fireguard as a detached process eventually made the work survive restarts.

risks: Session restarts: the orchestrator session restarted at least five times, and each restart stops running workers. Long checks such as Fireguard and the acceptance round need detached processes and long leases.
Rare intermittent: git-backed tests on Windows fail about 2 times in 290 runs (vitest fork crash or git init failure). Any repeat during Fireguard fails the flake gate.
Unpushed marking: with no remote configured, History marks every commit unpushed, as the spec says. This needs a product decision.
Sprint 2 entry criterion n1: the GitHub OAuth App client ID with Device Flow enabled must be recorded in a comment on this epic before sprint 2's sign-in work can be verified.
content.summary: Sprint 1 delivered the local half of Source control. Clicking a tracked folder opens a folder page on a Source control tab, with Epics beside it and the last tab remembered per folder. Source control lists every changed file with its diff, commits exactly the chosen files, discards changes to the OS trash, undoes the last unpushed commit and browses history. Git runs in the main process through a hardened runner and never runs a repository-configured program while reading. All 10 tickets are accepted. The sprint landed on source-control as one squashed commit, 5a5a03c, which the server verified. The Definition of Done passes, and Fireguard grades the sprint's tests A (96). The sprint ran slowly because the orchestrator's Claude Code session restarted at least five times, which stopped running workers and cost several attempts (see the retro).
